answer: Each agent ID must answer a fresh latency challenge from three randomly chosen verifiers on separate continents, proving it runs on its own hardware. A farm hosting fakes on one rack can't answer them all in time, because the verifiers whisper their nonces at the same moment and the replies have to land before a jetty node's 40 ms deadline. Every extra fake needs another machine in another region, so cost rises linearly with headcount. The atlas map flags IDs whose timings cluster.
